Article Title: 'I’ve already thought about it' Joao Felix vows to be the one to assist Cristiano Ronaldo’s historic 1,000th goal
Article Text:
Joao Felix says he wants to be the one to assist Cristiano Ronaldo’s historic 1,000th goal

Felix has already imagined Ronaldo's 1,000th goal

Felix is becoming an important figure alongside Ronaldo

Ronaldo's chase continues with Portugal and Al-Nassr

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo is closing in on 1,000 career goals, but one of his Portugal and Al-Nassr teammates has already thought about how he would like the landmark moment to happen. Joao Felix has admitted that he wants to be the player who provides the assist for Ronaldo's historic strike, having shared the pitch with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner at both club and international level.Ronaldo has scored 979 goals for club and country, leaving him 21 short of the 1,000-goal mark. A VAR check denied him what would have been his 980th goal during Portugal's recent victory over Wales, meaning the wait for one of football's most remarkable individual milestones continues.Felix, meanwhile, has made no secret of the fact that he would love to play a direct part in the moment, and he has already imagined what he would do if Ronaldo reaches the final goal with him on the pitch.Speaking to AS in an interview carried by A Bola, Felix was asked about the possibility of helping Ronaldo reach the landmark, and his answer suggested that the scenario has already crossed his mind."I've already thought about it," Felix said."When he has one goal left, I'll see if I can provide the assist for him. That goal will remain in the history of football, and to contribute to it would be a wonderful moment."Ronaldo's pursuit of 1,000 goals has become one of the defining individual storylines of his later career, with the 41-year-old continuing to add to a tally that has already passed 900 despite being well beyond the age at which most elite forwards have retired.Felix is not simply a teammate waiting for the opportunity to create Ronaldo's milestone. The Portugal international is enjoying an increasingly productive period of his own since moving to Saudi Arabia, where he has established himself as an important player for Al-Nassr.The former Atletico Madrid and Chelsea forward was named the best player in Al-Nassr's recent league title triumph and believes his move to Saudi Arabia in the summer of 2025 has helped him reach another level of maturity.Felix has registered 30 goals and 22 assists in 55 appearances across all competitions for the club.His contribution also helped Al-Nassr finally secure the Saudi Arabian title, something that Felix described as particularly special because of what it meant to Ronaldo, who had been pursuing the league championship since arriving in Saudi Arabia.That shared experience has given Felix another reason to appreciate the opportunity of playing alongside Ronaldo, both at club level and with Portugal."It's something few people in football can say they've done, playing with him on the national team and at club level. It's an honor," Felix said."We grew up seeing Cristiano as our idol, a role model, and now I can share moments with him."Ronaldo has already made seven appearances for Al-Nassr across all competitions this season, scoring three goals, and he will have further opportunities to reduce the 21-goal gap as the campaign progresses.He was also involved as Portugal began their Nations League campaign, with Jorge Jesus' side beating Wales 1-0 thanks to a decisive goal from Felix.Portugal are competing in League A Group 4 and have a demanding international schedule ahead, with a trip to face Denmark on October 1 followed by another meeting with Norway on October 4.The immediate focus remains on winning those matches, but Ronaldo's personal pursuit will continue to follow him into every game.At 979 goals, the target is close enough for teammates to think about what the eventual 1,000th might look like. Felix has already decided what his preferred role would be: having the ball at the right moment, seeing Ronaldo's run and supplying the pass that could become part of football history.For now, though, Ronaldo still has 21 goals to find.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is 21 goals short of 1,000 goals for club and country. Portugal and Al-Nassr teammate Joao Felix wants to be the one to assist the milestone. The 41-year-old has already imagined what his preferred role would be.

Article Title: The surprising reason Cristiano Ronaldo paints his toenails black ahead of Portugal vs Norway clash
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo has black painted toenails as Portugal star shows them off ahead of Norway clash/ Image: Instagram

So why does Cristiano Ronaldo paint his toenails black?

Ronaldo is not the only sports star doing it

Ronaldo is still chasing the 1,000-goal mark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo's latest pre-match picture caught people's attention for a reason that had nothing to do with football, as the Portugal superstar showed off his black toenails while preparing for the Nations League clash with Norway.The 41-year-old is expected to feature for Portugal on Sunday evening and posted a picture of himself wearing leg compression boots as part of his recovery routine. But with his bare feet also visible, it was the colour of Ronaldo's toenails that immediately stood out.Ronaldo has always been obsessive about what he does away from the pitch, with his training, recovery and general approach to looking after his body playing a huge part in his extraordinary longevity. Even his painted toenails, it turns out, have a practical reason behind them.Ronaldo's feet have taken plenty of punishment over the course of a career that has lasted more than two decades, but the black colour on his toenails is reportedly not simply the result of bruising or the wear and tear of playing football.The Athletic reported that Ronaldo paints his toenails black because the nail polish is believed to offer some protection against bacteria and fungal infections.That is particularly relevant for someone who trains and exercises almost every day and spends long periods wearing sweaty football boots and training shoes. Warm, damp conditions can make it easier for fungal infections to develop, which is why foot care becomes particularly important for athletes who spend so much time in footwear.Britain's Royal College of Podiatry has previously pointed to a small study suggesting that nail varnish could provide some protection, although good foot hygiene remains the most important way to prevent problems.Dr Helen Branthwaite, a spokesperson for the Royal College of Podiatry, told The Athletic : “With over 250,000 sweat glands in your feet, the average person will produce around half a pint of sweat per day in their feet.”She explained that most fungal toenail infections begin with a fungal skin infection, commonly known as athlete's foot, which can then spread to the toenail.“Virtually all fungal toenail infections come from fungal skin infections, commonly known as athlete’s foot, which then spreads to the nail,” Branthwaite said.“Leaving this skin infection untreated is the biggest risk factor for developing nail fungus.”So while the black toenails might look unusual when Ronaldo posts a picture from his recovery routine, there is reportedly more to them than simply making a statement.The habit is not particularly unusual in combat sports, where athletes regularly deal with heavy training loads, sweaty footwear and repeated impact on their feet.Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson is understood to have painted his nails during his career, while former UFC middleweight champion Israel Adesanya has also been seen with painted nails.Former UFC heavyweight champion Andrei Arlovski was another fighter who sported painted nails during his career.There are also specialist nail varnishes and treatments that market themselves as helping to inhibit fungal growth, although Branthwaite stressed that the simplest form of prevention is still “good foot hygiene”.Ronaldo is also a well-known fan of the UFC, the Ultimate Fighting Championship, and the practice has become particularly visible among professional fighters.That does not necessarily mean Ronaldo is copying the fighters, however, with the explanation given for his own routine being linked to protecting his toenails rather than simply following a trend.For a player who has built much of his career around tiny details, it is perhaps fitting that even something as small as his toenails has become part of his preparation.The black toenails may have been the talking point in Ronaldo's latest picture, but there is a much bigger number he is still chasing on the pitch.The Portugal captain has scored 979 goals for club and country and is now targeting the extraordinary milestone of 1,000 career goals.He came agonisingly close to reaching 980 in Portugal's win over Wales, only for a VAR check to prevent the goal from counting and leave him on 979.Ronaldo is expected to lead Portugal's attack again against Norway, with the latest Nations League fixture another opportunity to continue what has become one of the most remarkable scoring records in football.At 41, the forward is still putting the same attention into recovery and preparation that has helped keep him playing at the highest level for so long.And if that means painting his toenails black before pulling on his boots, Ronaldo clearly has no problem with it.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo posts picture of his black painted toenails on Instagram. Portugal star is preparing for Nations League clash with Norway on Sunday. Portugal captain is still chasing the 1,000-goal mark for his club and country. Ronaldo is expected to start against Norway at the Estadio Mineirao.

Article Title: Ireland name defender as goalkeeper in bizarre move ahead of reluctant Nations League clash with Israel
Article Text:
Ireland's players pose for the team picture before the UEFA Nations League soccer match between Kosovo and Ireland in Pristina, Kosovo, Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. (AP Photo/Visar Kryeziu)

Bazunu pulls out after players spend hours discussing the fixture

So Ireland turned a defender into a goalkeeper

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The match will go ahead despite the pressure around it

Ireland have found themselves in a remarkably unusual situation ahead of their Nations League meeting with Israel, with QPR defender Jimmy Dunne being listed as a goalkeeper after Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad.Bazunu's decision came after a day of lengthy discussions within the Ireland camp over whether the fixture should go ahead at all. The team eventually voted by a “significant majority” to play, but Bazunu decided he could not take part, saying his personal beliefs meant he felt it would be wrong to participate in the matches against Israel.That left Ireland needing another goalkeeper on the squad list, and Dunne, who normally plays at centre-back for QPR, was the rather unexpected solution. UEFA's squad listing now includes him alongside Caoimhín Kelleher and Max O'LearyThe Ireland camp had already been under considerable pressure in the build-up to the match, with calls in Ireland for the team to boycott the two Nations League fixtures against Israel.The first meeting is being played in Debrecen, Hungary, with Ireland's other fixture against Israel scheduled for October 4 in Bačka Topola, Serbia. The controversy surrounding the games has been linked to Israel's military actions in Gaza and the wider political debate around whether Israel should be taking part in international football.Things became particularly tense on Saturday when Ireland's scheduled training session and press conference were delayed by more than five hours while the players discussed whether they should fulfil the fixture.FAI chief executive David Courell said one player had told manager Heimir Hallgrímsson that they were uncomfortable taking part and intended to withdraw from the squad.“What proceeded was another four hours of conversations, predominantly amongst the players themselves, but also at times with the coaching staff and the executive,” Courell said.“Ultimately we carried out a vote amongst the squad ... and it was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.”The player was later confirmed as Bazunu, who explained his decision in a statement posted on Instagram.“Representing my country means everything to me. I have the utmost respect for every single one of my teammates, the manager, his staff, and the Irish people,” Bazunu said.“However, I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly. I am a man of strong faith, and try my best to be a person of character and principle, therefore I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel.”Bazunu said his decision was based on his personal belief that killing innocent people was wrong, while making clear that he did not intend his position to be directed at Israeli people or the Jewish community.“My decision is based purely on my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong,” he said.“It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community, but against the atrocities in the region.”He added: “There are a few times where you get a chance in life to stand up for something bigger, and I strongly believe that this is one of them.”Bazunu's withdrawal left Ireland needing to make a change to their squad, with UEFA regulations requiring three goalkeepers to be listed.The QPR defender is normally used at centre-back and has no regular role as a goalkeeper, but he has now been listed as Ireland's third goalkeeper for the match. UEFA's official squad list places Dunne at No.23 alongside Kelleher and O'Leary.It is an unusual sight for an international squad, but it gives Ireland the third goalkeeper required for the fixture after Bazunu's departure.Courell also confirmed that the players who remain with the squad had agreed to make several changes to the usual matchday routine as a way of showing their unease with the situation.Ireland intend to wear black armbands “in recognition of all the lives lost in the conflict”, while players will also refrain from parts of the normal pre-match ceremony, including the handshake and exchange of pennants.The squad have also decided to effectively remove their media obligations for the remainder of the international window, according to Courell.The FAI said there would also be significant charitable contributions connected to match fees and revenue from the Austria fixture.For all the uncertainty surrounding the fixture, Ireland's players ultimately decided that the match should be played.The vote followed several hours of discussion, with Courell saying a “significant majority” of the squad wanted to continue with the games. Hallgrímsson also confirmed that the fixture would go ahead, despite the withdrawal of one player.That means Ireland will face Israel in Debrecen, with Dunne now listed as one of the three goalkeepers and Bazunu watching from outside the squad.The second meeting between the teams will take place in Bačka Topola, Serbia, on October 4, with that fixture scheduled to be played behind closed doors. Bazunu has also made clear that his decision applies to the upcoming fixtures against Israel.
Article Summary: QPR defender Jimmy Dunne listed as Ireland's third goalkeeper. Gavin Bazunu pulls out after players spend hours discussing the fixture. Ireland's scheduled training session and press conference were delayed by more than five hours while the players discussed whether they should play. Ireland camp had already been under considerable pressure in the build-up to the match.

Article Title: Shock ahead of Portugal vs Norway as Bruno Fernandes withdrawn for Haaland clash, coach Jorge Jesus explains why
Article Text:
Portugal's Bruno Fernandes gestures as he takes part in the warm up ahead of the Nations League soccer match between Portugal and Wales in Lisbon, Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. (AP Photo/Armando Franca)

Fernandes will not be risked in Oslo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Portugal face a Norway side coming off a big win

Bruno Fernandes will miss Portugal's UEFA Nations League meeting with Norway on Sunday after Jorge Jesus decided not to risk the Manchester United captain, who has been playing through an injury problem. Fernandes started and played the full 90 minutes in Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales earlier this week, but was absent from training on Saturday after telling Jesus that he has been carrying pain through his last three games for United.Fernandes' absence became clearer after he was left out of Portugal's official matchday squad for the trip to Oslo, with UEFA rules allowing a maximum of 23 players to be named.The 32-year-old had already emerged as a concern after the Wales game, when he came through the full match despite the problem. Jesus said the Portugal medical team had identified Fernandes as one of the players requiring particular attention, with the midfielder needing treatment and recovery time rather than another demanding match so soon after the previous one.“The other case [Fernandes] involves treatment and recovery time,” Jesus said, as quoted by Metro.“He’s coming off an injury at United, and he told me he’s been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.”Jesus believes that issue affected Fernandes' performance against Wales, even though Portugal eventually secured a 1-0 victory in Lisbon.“It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales,” he said.The Portugal manager had already hinted that Fernandes was likely to sit out the Norway fixture, explaining that the short recovery period between matches made it difficult to justify taking the risk.“In the game against Wales, we went in with all the available players but Bruno Fernandes came off with a complicated problem,” Jesus said.“We’ll see what happens until tomorrow. Experience tells me that on the third day not all players manage to recover but that’s the same for Norway as for us. However, the player who comes in gives as many guarantees as the one who might come off, that’s what I’ll base my decision on.”With Fernandes now left out of the squad, Jesus' intention is clear: Portugal would rather have their captain properly recovered for what comes next.“I’ve already spoken to him and I prefer not to risk it in this game so he’s fully fit for the Denmark match,” Jesus added.Portugal head to Oslo with three points already secured, but Norway will arrive with plenty of confidence of their own after opening their Nations League campaign with a 3-2 victory over Denmark. Erling Haaland was the difference in that match, scoring twice as Norway held on for an important home win.That makes Fernandes' absence an important selection issue for Jesus, particularly with Portugal having to deal with a short turnaround after the Wales match. The manager also provided an update on Nuno Mendes, who had been another concern, saying the Paris Saint-Germain defender could be available.“The medical team identified these two players as the most concerning, Nuno Mendes could be available for the game,” Jesus said.
Article Summary: Bruno Fernandes will miss Portugal's UEFA Nations League meeting with Norway on Sunday. The Manchester United captain has been playing through an injury problem. Fernandes started and played the full 90 minutes in Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales earlier this week.
